items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: Dewey Redman and Don Pullen they were very big mentors to me and they were probably two of the heaviest musicians sort of out there on the scene. And they were so encouraging to me.

ctx.x: You’re in Toronto and I’m at Hamilton College in Clinton, New York, and I’m going to introduce you as a soprano saxophonist, a flute player, band leader, and an expert on work visas and passports from other countries. That must be tough.

Yeah it has been, you know, to do all — you know it’s hard enough touring but to do all the extra work that, you know, that we’ve had to do to get people, you know, into Canada, into the U.S. It’s been an ongoing thing for probably forty-something years. I mean our first time, Larry and mine — my partner, trumpet playing producer husband first went to Cuba I guess ’81, ’82 and that’s when we sort of got very, you know, it was a huge surprise going to Cuba and, you know hearing the music that we were hearing and…

Can I ask you about the learning process, being a schooled musician, that’s such a — not a helpful term but I’ll use it anyway — learning the Latin rhythms and making them rhythmically become inside you. Did you try to figure it out from actually like transcribing things?
